name: John G. Roberts Jr.
title: Chief Justice
bio: Chief Justice Roberts has served as the 17th Chief Justice of the United States since 2005. Before his appointment, he served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit.

key_rulings.description: Upheld the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate as a valid exercise of Congress's taxing power.
Struck down Section 4(b) of the Voting Rights Act, ruling the coverage formula unconstitutional.

key_rulings.case: Department of Commerce v. New York
key_rulings.description: Blocked the Trump administration from adding a citizenship question to the 2020 census.
Concurred with the majority opinion overturning Roe v. Wade, ending federal constitutional right to abortion.

career.role: Special Assistant to the Attorney General

career.org: U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit

controversies.title: Undisclosed Federalist Society Trip
controversies.description: ProPublica reported Roberts attended a Federalist Society fishing trip in Alaska paid for by Republican donors, not initially disclosed.

controversies.title: Recusal Refusal on Congressional Subpoena
controversies.description: Roberts declined a Senate Judiciary Committee invitation to testify on SCOTUS ethics, citing separation of powers concerns.

controversies.title: Wife's Legal Recruiting Fees
controversies.description: Jane Roberts earned $10.3M in legal recruiting fees from firms that have cases before SCOTUS, raising conflict of interest questions.

name: Clarence Thomas
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Thomas has served on the Supreme Court since 1991, making him the longest-serving current justice. He is known for his originalist interpretation of the Constitution.

key_rulings.description: Concurred that the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms applies to state and local governments.
Concurred, arguing that substantive due process precedents should be reconsidered.

key_rulings.case: New York State Rifle & Pistol Assn. v. Bruen
key_rulings.description: Struck down New York's concealed carry permit law, expanding gun rights.

key_rulings.case: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
key_rulings.description: Concurred in striking down affirmative action in college admissions.

career.org: U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit

controversies.title: Harlan Crow Real Estate & Luxury Gifts ($4M+)
controversies.description: ProPublica revealed Thomas accepted over $4M in undisclosed luxury travel and gifts from Republican megadonor Harlan Crow, including private jet trips, superyacht voyages, and private school tuition for Thomas's grandnephew. Crow also purchased Thomas's mother's home.

controversies.title: Anthony Welters Private Jet Flights (Unreported)
controversies.description: Additional unreported private jet travel from health care executive Anthony Welters, who had business before the federal government.

controversies.title: Ginni Thomas January 6th Texts
controversies.description: Thomas's wife Virginia 'Ginni' Thomas sent texts urging White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows to overturn the 2020 election. Thomas refused to recuse himself from Jan. 6-related cases.

controversies.title: Anita Hill Confirmation Hearing
controversies.description: Anita Hill testified under oath that Thomas sexually harassed her while she was his employee at the EEOC. Thomas denied all allegations and was confirmed 52–48.

controversies.title: 20+ Years of Unreported Gifts
controversies.description: Thomas failed to report Harlan Crow gifts on required financial disclosure forms for over two decades, in apparent violation of federal disclosure law.

name: Samuel A. Alito Jr.
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Alito has served on the Supreme Court since 2006. Prior to his appointment, he served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit.

key_rulings.description: Ruled that corporate funding of independent political broadcasts cannot be limited under the First Amendment.
Ruled that closely held corporations can be exempt from laws for religious reasons.
Authored the majority opinion overturning Roe v. Wade and Planned Parenthood v. Casey.
Ruled that public school coach could pray on the field after games.

controversies.title: Upside-Down American Flag After January 6
controversies.description: An upside-down American flag — a symbol used by Stop the Steal movement — was flown at Alito's Virginia home in January 2021, days after the Capitol riot. Alito blamed his wife but refused to recuse from Jan. 6 cases.

controversies.title: Appeal to Heaven Flag
controversies.description: An 'Appeal to Heaven' flag — associated with Christian nationalism and January 6 rioters — was flown at Alito's New Jersey vacation home. Alito again refused to recuse.

controversies.title: Paul Singer Undisclosed Trips
controversies.description: ProPublica reported Alito took an undisclosed luxury fishing trip to Alaska in 2008 with hedge fund billionaire Paul Singer, whose firm later had business before SCOTUS. Alito did not recuse himself.

name: Sonia Sotomayor
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Sotomayor became the first Latina Supreme Court Justice when she was appointed in 2009. She previously served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.

key_rulings.case: Schuette v. Coalition to Defend Affirmative Action
key_rulings.description: Dissented from upholding Michigan's ban on affirmative action in higher education.
Dissented from allowing evidence from illegal stops to be used in court.
Dissented from upholding the Trump administration's travel ban.
Joined the dissent opposing the overturning of Roe v. Wade.

controversies.title: 'Wise Latina' Controversy
controversies.description: A 2001 speech in which Sotomayor said a 'wise Latina woman' might reach better decisions than a white male drew criticism during her confirmation hearings. She called it a poor word choice.

name: Elena Kagan
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Kagan has served on the Supreme Court since 2010. Before her appointment, she served as the U.S. Solicitor General and was the first woman to serve as Dean of Harvard Law School.

key_rulings.case: National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius
key_rulings.description: Dissented in part, arguing the entire Affordable Care Act should be upheld.
Joined the majority legalizing same-sex marriage nationwide.
Dissented from ruling that public sector unions cannot collect fees from non-members.
Joined the dissent opposing the overturning of Roe v. Wade.

name: Neil M. Gorsuch
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Gorsuch has served on the Supreme Court since 2017. He previously served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit and is known for his textualist approach to statutory interpretation.

key_rulings.description: Authored majority opinion ruling that Title VII protects LGBTQ employees from discrimination.
Ruled that much of eastern Oklahoma remains Native American territory.

key_rulings.case: New York State Rifle & Pistol Assn. v. Bruen
key_rulings.description: Joined the majority striking down New York's concealed carry permit law.

key_rulings.case: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
key_rulings.description: Joined the majority striking down affirmative action in college admissions.

career.org: Justice Byron White & Justice Anthony Kennedy, SCOTUS
Kellogg, Huber, Hansen, Todd, Evans & Figel

controversies.title: Stolen Seat — Merrick Garland Block
controversies.description: Gorsuch fills the seat Senate Republicans refused to consider for Merrick Garland (Obama's nominee) for 10 months before the 2016 election — an unprecedented partisan obstruction.

controversies.title: Real Estate Sale to Law Firm Client
controversies.description: Gorsuch sold a 40-acre property to the CEO of a law firm that had cases before SCOTUS, two weeks after his confirmation. Not disclosed until ProPublica's investigation.

name: Brett M. Kavanaugh
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Kavanaugh has served on the Supreme Court since 2018. He previously served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit for 12 years.

key_rulings.description: Dissented from striking down Louisiana abortion clinic restrictions.
Ruled the Biden administration could end the 'Remain in Mexico' immigration policy.
Concurred with overturning Roe v. Wade.
Struck down President Biden's student loan forgiveness plan.

career.org: Judge Alex Kozinski, 9th Circuit; Justice Anthony Kennedy, SCOTUS
U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit

controversies.title: Christine Blasey Ford Sexual Assault Allegation
controversies.description: Dr. Christine Blasey Ford testified under oath that Kavanaugh sexually assaulted her at a high school party in 1982. Kavanaugh denied it. An FBI investigation was limited in scope. He was confirmed 50–48.

controversies.title: Deborah Ramirez and Julie Swetnick Allegations
controversies.description: Two additional women — Deborah Ramirez (Yale classmate) and Julie Swetnick — made sexual misconduct allegations. The FBI did not investigate Ramirez's claim despite her witness list.

controversies.title: Perjury Allegations Over Pre-Confirmation Statements
controversies.description: Multiple former colleagues contradicted Kavanaugh's sworn testimony about his knowledge of Democratic memos during his time as a Bush White House aide. Critics alleged perjury.

name: Amy Coney Barrett
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Barrett has served on the Supreme Court since 2020. She previously served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit and taught at Notre Dame Law School.

key_rulings.case: Americans for Prosperity Foundation v. Bonta
key_rulings.description: Ruled California cannot require charities to disclose major donors.
Concurred with overturning Roe v. Wade.
Joined the majority striking down student loan forgiveness.

key_rulings.case: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
key_rulings.description: Joined the majority striking down affirmative action in college admissions.

controversies.title: Rushed Confirmation — 27 Days Before Election
controversies.description: Barrett was confirmed 52–48 on Oct. 26, 2020 — 8 days before the election — after Republicans refused to consider Merrick Garland 10 months before the 2016 election, citing the 'Biden Rule.'

controversies.title: People of Praise Membership
controversies.description: Barrett's membership in the charismatic Catholic group 'People of Praise,' which has traditional views on gender roles, raised questions during confirmation. Barrett declined to discuss it in detail.

name: Ketanji Brown Jackson
title: Associate Justice
bio: Justice Jackson became the first Black woman to serve on the Supreme Court when she was appointed in 2022. She previously served on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit and the U.S. District Court for D.C.

key_rulings.case: Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard
key_rulings.description: Dissented from striking down affirmative action, emphasizing the importance of diversity.
Dissented from striking down student loan forgiveness.
Dissented from ruling allowing businesses to refuse service based on religious objections.
Concurred in rejecting the 'independent state legislature theory' for elections.

career.org: U.S. Court of Appeals, D.C. Circuit

controversies.title: Sentencing Criticism from Republicans
controversies.description: Republicans attacked Jackson during confirmation over sentencing decisions in child pornography cases, alleging she was too lenient. Legal experts said her sentences were in line with similar judges.
